prs.title: fix(formatter): decide embedded template layout from AST, not source shape
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Closes #21908 The layout of an embedded template (`` css`...` ``, etc) as a sole call argument or an arrow body was decided by its source shape. Since the content is rewritten, the same input could get different layouts depending on how it was formatted, and some cases were not idempotent. Now: - `embeddedLanguageFormatting: off`: verbatim template rule, as before - whitespace-only embedded templates are also now kept as-is, like Prettier - Otherwise, an embed target is detected from the AST (`embed_hug()`), regardless of whether its content formats - Sole argument: last-arg expansion (hug if the first line fits, otherwise break the args) - Arrow body: hug (except whitespace-sensitive HTML) NOTE: `openclaw` repo in ecosystem-ci report a lot of diffs like: ```ts // main (entry) => html`
  • ...
    • `, // This PR (entry) => html`
  • ...
    • `, ``` But this is the same behavior with Prettier 3.9.9.

prs.title: perf(lexer): make `run == 3` operator arm branchless
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

When `coalesce` meets a run of exactly 3 operator characters, it has to decide between 4 outcomes:

1. One 3-byte operator.
2. 2-byte operator then a 1-byte one.
3. 1-byte operator then a 2-byte one.
4. Three 1-byte operators.

Previously it worked out how far to advance with a chain of `if`s, which the compiler turned into a branch on whether the 3-byte lookup matched. That's unpredictable in minified code (`===` and `...` match, `&&!` and `||!` don't).

This PR rewrites the selection as two booleans. "the token at `p` covers `p + 1`" and "`p + 2` is inside a multi-byte token".

The cursor then becomes `p + 2 + c2`. The branch disappears and the block is roughly 20 instructions shorter on x86_64.

prs.title: perf(lexer): unroll loop in `opmap_longest`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

`opmap_longest` tried lengths 4, 3 and 2 in a loop, using the hash table for each.

There's only one 4-byte operator (`>>>=`), so check for it with a plain 4-byte compare, then do the 3-byte and 2-byte lookups explicitly, instead of looping.

This has 3 effects:

- Removes branches wherever `opmap_longest` is inlined (2 in `munch_walk`, 11 in `step_op`),
- Simplifies the perfect hash checks, since there are no longer any 4-byte cases to guard against.
- `len` is now statically known everywhere in `opmap_lookup`, so the mask in `op_key` is an immediate value, not calculated.

prs.title: perf(lexer): remove cap on `max_len` for `opmap_longest`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Small perf optimization.

#27062 removed the loop from `opmap_longest`, so it doesn't calculate `len` from `max_len` any more. There's no longer a need for callers to clamp the value to max 4, so remove that code.

prs.title: perf(lexer): do not include length in operator hash map key
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

The hash key for operators hash table included the candidate's length in its top byte.

#27062 made `opmap_lookup` no longer handle 4-bytes operators via the hash table, so now storing the length in the key is redundant. An operator's bytes already tell you its length, as 2-byte operators are stored with a zero 3rd byte, and no 3-byte operator contains a zero byte.

Dropping it saves an instruction per key in `coalesce`'s hot path.

The one catch is that a 3-byte candidate whose 3rd byte is `\0` now has exactly the same key as the matching 2-byte operator (e.g. `==\0` and `==`), so `opmap_lookup` rejects that case explicitly. It can only happen with a `\0` byte in the source, which is a syntax error anyway, so the branch is never taken in practice.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): introduce `OpTable` abstraction
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Pure refactor.

Introduce `OpTable` struct which stores the hash table's data and multiplier. Move lookup logic into methods of this type.

The table data lives in a `static` (`OpTableData`), and `OpTable` is a `const` that points to it, so the multiplier compiles down to a constant at usage sites, and it doesn't take up any space in the binary.

This prepares the way for the next 2 PRs - #27066 and #27067.

prs.title: perf(lexer): align operator hash table to cache lines
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Small perf optimization.

Align the operator hash table to 128 bytes, so it occupies the fewest possible cache lines:

- 2 x 128-byte lines on Apple Silicon.
- 2 x aligned pairs of 64-byte lines on x86_64 (where the CPU fetches lines in pairs).

prs.title: perf(lexer): split operator hash table into two
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

Split the operator hash table into 2 separate tables for 2-byte and 3-byte operators.

- 2-byte table = 32 slots = 128 bytes.
- 3-byte table = 16 slots = 64 bytes.

Total is 192 bytes, down from 256. Each table is aligned so it fills whole cache lines.

Because each table now only holds operators of a specific length, a lookup can never match an operator of a different length. That makes the `\0` check added in #27064 unnecessary, so it can be removed.

It also lets `coalesce` compare 2-byte operators with a single 16-bit comparison. This turns 3 x 2-byte operator checks in `coalesce` from 3 instructions (copy, mask, compare) into 1 (`cmp cx, ax`).

prs.title: perf(lexer): reduce branches in `opmap_longest`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization.

Make `OpTable::lookup` return `Option<u32>` instead of using 0 to mean "not found".

`opmap_longest` can then branch on whether the lookup matched, rather than testing the kind for 0 again afterwards.

- `opmap_longest` goes from 7 branches to 4.
- `munch_walk` is 3 instructions shorter.
- `step_op` is ~200 instructions shorter (compiler was duplicating code to work around the branch structure).

For this to be correct, a lookup must never report an empty slot as a match. The only key that could do that is all zeros, which always hashes to slot 0. `test_perfect_hash` test checks that slot 0 is occupied in both tables, so the "matched" branch can never produce `0` as the kind.

prs.title: perf(lexer): `opmap_longest` return `Option<TokenKind>`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Small perf optimization.

Continuation of #27068. Make `opmap_longest` return `Option<TokenKind>` instead of a `u32`.

Each return path then tells the compiler whether an operator was found, so `munch_walk` no longer has to test the kind for 0 after the call.

`munch_walk` loses 2 branches and 5 instructions.

prs.title: perf(lexer): reduce branches in `op_len`
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Tiny optimization.

`op_len` calls `opmap_longest` to find out if 4 bytes at a position `pos` comprise an operator. It capped the operator search to `self.n - pos` bytes, where `self.n` is the length of source (unpadded length).

The cap is always >= 4 except at the very end of source, when some of `bytes` contains `\0` padding bytes after end of source.

Remove the cap, and just pass `4` as `max_len`. `opmap_longest` then unconditionally checks for 4-byte, 3-byte, and 2-byte operators. The result is the same - when at end of source, `bytes` contains some `\0` padding bytes, which can't match any operator.

This reduces work in the common case where _not_ at the end of source, in return for a few more operations in the very uncommon case of being at very end of source.

This removes 8 instructions, 1 load (`self.n`), and 1 branch from `op_len`.

Note: We can't do the same at `opmap_longest`'s other call site in `munch_walk`, as there passing the correct `max_len` is required for correctness (avoid incorrectly combining `>`s in some cases).

This is cold path code, so makes little practical difference, but why not?

prs.title: feat(minifier): merge import and export statements against the same module
prs.author: sapphi-red
prs.body:
Compress
```js
import { b, g } from "./res-SWvxTGCX.js";
export { g as load_css, b as start };
```

to
```js
export { g as load_css, b as start } from "./res-SWvxTGCX.js";
```

Some combinations (e.g. namespace + named specifier) are not allowed in `export`s while it's allowed in `import`s, so that part should be reviewed with caution.

Note that `just minsize` result does not change because the input does not contain any import / exports.

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/no-zero-fractions): parenthesize separator and large integers in fixer
prs.author: breken-ai
prs.body:
### Bug

When `unicorn/no-zero-fractions` removes the fraction from a number that is the object of a member access, the fix adds parentheses so the result stays valid (`1.00.toFixed(2)` becomes `(1).toFixed(2)`). It decides whether parentheses are needed with `fmt.parse::<i64>()`, which fails for integers that contain numeric separators or don't fit in an `i64`. Those cases get no parentheses, so the fix produces a syntax error:

```js
1_000.0.toFixed(2)                   // fixed to `1_000.toFixed(2)`: SyntaxError
10000000000000000000.0.toFixed(2)    // fixed to `10000000000000000000.toFixed(2)`: SyntaxError
```

The linter's own fixer test catches this: `Linter fixer produced invalid syntax ... Invalid characters after number`.

### Fix

A literal needs the parentheses when the fixed text is only digits and `_`. That matches the decimal-integer check in eslint-plugin-unicorn, which accepts separators. Exponent forms such as `1e10.toFixed()` stay unparenthesized, as they are today.

### Tests

I added two `expect_fix` cases (`1_000.0.toFixed(2)` and a 20-digit integer). Both fail on `main` with the invalid-syntax panic and pass with the fix. `cargo test -p oxc_linter --lib unicorn` passes (148 tests) and `cargo clippy -p oxc_linter --lib --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

I used AI assistance (Claude) to prepare this change, then reviewed and tested it myself.

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/numeric-separators-style): report misgrouped BigInt literals
prs.author: breken-ai
prs.body:
### Bug

`unicorn/numeric-separators-style` checks number literals with `formatted != raw`, but for BigInt literals it only compares lengths: `formatted.len() != number.span.size()`. A BigInt with the same number of separators in the wrong places has the same length as the correct form, so it is never reported:

```js
const a = 12_34_567;   // reported, fixed to 1_234_567
const b = 12_34_567n;  // not reported (should become 1_234_567n)
const c = 0xA_BCDn;    // not reported (should become 0xAB_CDn)
```

### Fix

Compare the formatted BigInt with its raw text, as the number branch already does. `format_bigint` keeps the prefix, digit case and `n` suffix as they were, so a correctly grouped literal still matches exactly.

### Tests

I added `12_34_567n` and `0xA_BCDn` to the fail and fix cases and updated the snapshot. On `main` both are "expected to fail, but passed" with no fix applied. With this change they are reported and fixed. `cargo test -p oxc_linter --lib unicorn` passes (148 tests) and `cargo clippy -p oxc_linter --lib --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

I used AI assistance (Claude) to prepare this change, then reviewed and tested it myself.

fix(oxfmt): do not re-include a file below an excluded directory with a negated pattern
prs.author: KuSh
prs.body:
## Summary

A negated pattern no longer re-includes a file whose parent directory is excluded, for explicit paths, `--stdin-filepath` and the language server. This is what the directory walk, Git and Prettier already do.

With `.prettierignore`:

```
vendor/
!vendor/keep.ts
```

`oxfmt .` skips `vendor/keep.ts` (the walk prunes `vendor/`), but `oxfmt vendor/keep.ts`, `--stdin-filepath vendor/keep.ts` and format-on-save formatted it. The explicit-path checks call `Gitignore::matched_path_or_any_parents()`, which matches the path itself first: `!vendor/keep.ts` is a whitelist match and the parent directory is never consulted. The same applied to `ignorePatterns` in `.oxfmtrc.json`.

Git documents the rule: "It is not possible to re-include a file if a parent directory of that file is excluded."

## Measured behaviour

Formatted = the file is formatted, ignored = it is skipped. Git column is `git check-ignore` with the same patterns as `.gitignore`. Prettier is 3.9.9 (the version pinned in `apps/oxfmt/package.json`).

| Patterns (`.prettierignore`) | File | git | CLI walk | CLI explicit / stdin / LSP, before | CLI explicit / stdin / LSP, after | Prettier `.` / explicit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: `vendor/`, `!vendor/keep.ts` | `vendor/keep.ts` | ignored | ignored | formatted | ignored | ignored / ignored |
| B: `vendor/*`, `!vendor/keep.ts` | `vendor/keep.ts` | not ignored | formatted | formatted | formatted | formatted / formatted |
| C: `*.gen.ts`, `!kee
